sentences.text: Tuojiangosaurus was a herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur that grew to a length of 6.5 to 7 meters and weighed approximately 2.8 metric tons.
Its lower jaw contained at least twenty-five teeth, each featuring a thick base with a cingulum merging into a triangular vertical median ridge.
In 1990, Galton identified a unique trait where the tail base vertebrae spines possessed bony skirts running from the front to the sides.
Later, in 2006, Maidment and Wei identified two additional diagnostic characters: frontal bones wider than long and well-separated ilium processes.
Dong estimated that the animal had about seventeen pairs of plates and spikes along its back and tail.
The arrangement of tail spikes in this dinosaur is affectionately known as the "thagomizer".
Paul interpreted these tail spikes as a "pin-cushion array" based on a specimen of Chungkingosaurus.
Remains of a stegosaurian were discovered in 1974 during the construction of the Wujiaba dam in Zigong, Sichuan.
The fossils were recovered from the upper portion of the Shangshaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China, specifically from the holotype specimen CV 209.
This holotype specimen CV 209 dates to the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages of the Upper Shaximiao Formation.
The species Tuojiangosaurus multispinus was named in 1977 by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, Li Xuanmin, and Chang Yijong based on two specimens.
The generic name Tuojiangosaurus is derived from the Tuo River near the holotype's discovery site, while the specific name multispinus comes from Latin words for "many" and "spine".
Additional material, including juveniles, has been referred to the species since the initial discovery.
Tuojiangosaurus fed on low-lying ground vegetation.
Due to lacking high dorsal spines for muscle insertion found in Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus probably could not stand upright on its hind legs.
Tuojiangosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
The parent group for the genus Tuojiangosaurus is Stegosauridae.
Dong originally classified Tuojiangosaurus in the subfamily Stegosaurinae of the family Stegosauridae in 1977.
A 2004 cladistic analysis by Galton placed Tuojiangosaurus in a derived position as the sister species of Chialingosaurus.

A 2009 analysis by Mateus, Maidment, and Christiansen found that Tuojiangosaurus fell outside the family Stegosauridae, though its exact position within Stegosauria remained uncertain due to fragmentary remains.
A more complete 2017 analysis by Raven and Maidment found that Tuojiangosaurus grouped with Huayangosaurus and its relatives.
Tuojiangosaurus lived at the end of the Jurassic Period, approximately 160 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
Tuojiangosaurus lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, approximately 168.2 to 161.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Tuojiangosaurus is an early or late branching member of Stegosauria, as some analyses place it outside Stegosauridae due to fragmentary remains.
